query: What signals suggest an incident resolution will be inefficient?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Category of the incident (printer, network, etc.) is known at intake and plausibly correlates with resolution difficulty; lies outside the focus variable.

per_column.name: reassignment_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether the ticket was reassigned is itself a hallmark of an inefficient handling process. It typically only becomes known during/after resolution and is largely a component of what 'inefficient resolution' means, so it leaks the outcome rather than predicting it independently.

per_column.name: hardware_failure_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity of the underlying hardware fault is an intrinsic property of the problem, knowable early, and plausibly drives how hard/slow resolution is without restating the outcome.

per_column.name: affected_asset_type
per_column.rationale: Type of asset (printer, server, laptop) is an intake attribute that plausibly carries signal about resolution effort; outside the focus and non-deterministic of it.

per_column.name: shared_vs_personal_asset
per_column.rationale: Whether the asset is shared or personally assigned is a stable attribute known upfront; shared assets may involve coordination/access issues affecting efficiency. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: repeat_incident_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether this is a recurring incident is knowable from history at intake and is a plausible driver of harder/slower resolution without restating the outcome.

judge.rationale: Five of six columns are legitimate, intake-time predictors describing the nature of the incident and asset (category, asset type, severity, shared/personal, repeat status), giving a model meaningful leverage beyond the original scheduling/identity fields. However, incident_category and affected_asset_type are near-duplicates of each other, reducing independent signal, and reassignment_signal leaks the outcome since reassignment is a core marker/component of inefficient resolution and is only known during processing. The set carries moderate genuine predictive value.
